title: Split 'conversion' into pricing-page reach, pricing to checkout, checkout to paid
decision_task: When the computed constraint is conversion for a self-serve product, which part of the purchase path to fix first.
applies_when: Self-serve paid plans with a pricing page and online checkout
Conversion flagged as the weak link
exclusions: Quote-based or custom-priced sales (use sales-stage logic)
Too few pricing-page visitors to read the link rates: use a heuristic review instead
Local services that sell by call or booking
required_inputs: Page and checkout events, or owner counts from site analytics and billing
evidence_requirements: Share of signups who view pricing
Unique pricing visitors who start checkout
Which in-product triggers lead to upgrade
missing_data_behavior: No pricing-path counts: first step collects them; meanwhile a heuristic pricing-page review only.
Too few pricing-page visitors: heuristic review, no rate comparison.
alternatives_when_constrained: Low traffic: heuristic page review and 3–5 user walkthroughs
Missing data: site analytics page views plus billing export

decision_branches.then: Contextual upgrade prompts at the moment of need.
Fix checkout failures (payment methods, errors, surprises).

implementation_steps: Compute the three link rates for one cohort
Low awareness: add contextual upsells where each paid feature is hit in the product
Low pricing-to-checkout: review structure (about three plans, clear value metric, recommended plan, who each plan is for, accumulating features, price visible, pricing in navigation)
Low checkout completion: check payment methods, currency and billing timing
Consider add-ons for features few customers on a plan use
Change one thing for new buyers and read it via PB-pricing-test
dependencies: Analytics on pricing page and checkout
guardrails: No decoy tiers or hidden costs (existing PB-pricing-test guardrail)
Plan labels such as 'most popular' must be true
observation_window: Whole weeks until each link has a readable count; for price changes use PB-pricing-test's window.
stop_conditions: Fixed link improves but paid conversion is flat: the constraint moved, recompute
review_triggers: Owner corrects an input this playbook relies on
A metric or guardrail crosses its bound
The underlying source or platform rule changes
climbos_location: shared/agents/diagnosis.ts 'purchase' reading and playStage 'conversion'; PB-pricing-test in shared/playbooks/contracts.ts.

interpretation: INTERPRETATION: ClimbOS's conversion branch currently goes straight to package or price. Many self-serve conversion problems are discovery or checkout problems that a price test would not fix.
proposed_climbos_rule: PROPOSED RULE: When conversion binds for a self-serve type and pricing-path counts exist, compute the three sub-links and require the bankable play to target the weakest. If counts are missing, the first step collects them. PB-pricing-test is preferred only when pricing-to-checkout is the weak sub-link.
disagreements: None with the library. Her case for public prices in B2B may conflict with owners running custom quotes; treat as a test, not a rule.

hypothetical_evaluation_cases.label: hypothetical
expected_behavior: Identifies awareness (8% of signups see pricing) as the weak link while pricing-to-checkout and checkout completion look healthy
Proposes contextual upsells, not a price cut
Labels Verna's 25%/25%/50% as unsourced 2024 author benchmarks
hard_failure: Discounts price as the first move
Treats her benchmarks as reliable industry norms

notes: Proposed reference contract. Not executable; does not authorize publishing, sending or spending. Numbers in source references are dated author figures, never forecasts.
